page: Vultr vcg-a40-12c-60g-24vram is a virtual machine in the Cloud GPU family. It features a fractional NVIDIA A40 GPU representing a half-slice allocation with 24 GB of Ampere-architecture VRAM. The host system is powered by an Intel Xeon x86_64 processor configured with 12 shared vCPUs, which map to 6 physical cores and 2 threads per core running at a base speed of 2.0 GHz. System memory totals 60.0 GB, yielding 5.0 GB per core, and local storage is provided by a 1110 GB NVMe SSD.

Benchmark data places this server in the average tier across most performance metrics. The stress-ng single-core CPU performance is 1631.08, and multi-core performance reaches 20624.31. Memory bandwidth tests show 1186.32 GB/sec for cached small blocks, dropping to 123.01 GB/sec for large uncached reads and 53.08 GB/sec for large uncached writes. In LLM inference testing, the system handles a small 135M model efficiently, achieving 1048.4 tokens/sec for prompt processing and 219.1 tokens/sec for text generation. However, performance drops significantly on larger models; prompt processing for a medium 7B model falls into the bottom 25% tier at 23.45 tokens/sec, though text generation remains average at 9.43 tokens/sec.

From a cost efficiency perspective, the fractional GPU allocation allows users to access enterprise-grade Ampere hardware and 24 GB VRAM without paying for a full dedicated GPU. The primary tradeoff is the shared CPU allocation and a moderate 2.0 GHz clock speed, which limits raw single-threaded compute performance. This configuration is suitable for workloads such as small-to-medium LLM inference, moderate machine learning training, database operations supported by 1110 GB NVMe storage and a PassMark database score of 5563.82, and static web serving.
description: Vultr vcg-a40-12c-60g-24vram is a Cloud GPU server featuring a fractional NVIDIA A40 GPU with 24 GB of VRAM, paired with 12 shared Intel Xeon vCPUs running at 2.0 GHz. The system includes 60.0 GB of system memory and 1110 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. Benchmark results show average performance across most categories, including a stress-ng multi-core score of 20624.31 and a PassMark CPU score of 20613.93. LLM inference benchmarks reveal a clear tradeoff: the server processes small 135M models efficiently at 1048.4 tokens/sec for prompts, but performance drops to a weak 23.45 tokens/sec for medium 7B model prompts. This instance provides a cost-efficient entry point for GPU-accelerated workloads, making it suitable for small-scale machine learning inference, database operations, and general-purpose applications requiring moderate GPU acceleration and local NVMe storage.
